sections.section_title: Short title, extent and commencement
sections.text: This Act may be called the Limitation Act, 1963. It extends to the whole of India and shall come into force on the first day of January, 1964.
sections.chapter: I — Preliminary

sections.section_title: Definitions
sections.text: In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires, (a) 'applicant' includes any person from or through whom an applicant derives his right to apply; (b) 'defendant' includes any person from or through whom a defendant derives his liability to be sued; (c) 'plaintiff' includes any person from or through whom a plaintiff derives his right to sue; (d) 'period of limitation' means the period of limitation prescribed for any suit, appeal or application by the Schedule; (e) 'prescribed' means prescribed by the Schedule; (f) 'tort' means a civil wrong which is not exclusively a breach of contract or a breach of trust; (g) 'trust' includes a fiduciary relationship.
sections.chapter: I — Preliminary

sections.section_title: Bar of limitation
sections.text: Subject to the provisions contained in sections 4 to 24, every suit instituted, appeal preferred, or application made after the prescribed period shall be dismissed, although limitation has not been set up as a defence.
sections.chapter: II — Limitation of Suits, Appeals and Applications

sections.section_title: Expiry of prescribed period when court is closed
sections.text: Where the prescribed period for any suit, appeal or application expires on a day when the court is closed, the suit, appeal or application may be instituted, preferred or made on the day when the court reopens.
sections.chapter: II — Limitation of Suits, Appeals and Applications

sections.section_title: Extension of prescribed period in certain cases
sections.text: Any appeal or application for a review of judgment or for leave to appeal or any other application to which this section may be made applicable may be admitted after the prescribed period if the appellant or applicant satisfies the court that he had sufficient cause for not preferring the appeal or making the application within such period.
sections.chapter: II — Limitation of Suits, Appeals and Applications

sections.section_title: Legal disability
sections.text: Where a person entitled to institute a suit or make an application is, at the time from which the prescribed period is to be reckoned, a minor or insane, or an idiot, he may institute the suit or make the application within the same period after the disability has ceased, as would otherwise have been allowed from the time prescribed.
sections.chapter: II — Limitation of Suits, Appeals and Applications

sections.section_title: Disability of one of several plaintiffs or applicants
sections.text: Where one of several persons jointly entitled to institute a suit or make an application is under a disability, and a discharge can be given without the concurrence of that person, time will run against them all; but where no such discharge can be given, time will not run until the disability has ceased.
sections.chapter: II — Limitation of Suits, Appeals and Applications

sections.section_title: Special exceptions
sections.text: Nothing in section 6 or section 7 applies to suits to enforce rights of pre-emption, or shall be deemed to extend the period of limitation for any suit or application beyond the period of three years from the cessation of the disability or the death of the person affected.
sections.chapter: II — Limitation of Suits, Appeals and Applications

sections.section_title: Continuous running of time
sections.text: Where once time has begun to run, no subsequent disability or inability to institute a suit or make an application stops it.
sections.chapter: II — Limitation of Suits, Appeals and Applications

sections.section_title: Suits against trustees and their representatives
sections.text: No suit against a person in whom property has become vested in trust for any specific purpose, or against his legal representatives or assigns, shall be barred by any length of time for the reason that the property has been received and converted to his own use.
sections.chapter: II — Limitation of Suits, Appeals and Applications

sections.section_title: Suits on contracts entered into outside the territories to which the Act extends
sections.text: Suits instituted in India on contracts entered into outside the territories to which this Act extends shall be subject to the period of limitation applicable under the law in force in the place where the contract was made, provided that the period does not exceed the period prescribed by the Schedule.
sections.chapter: II — Limitation of Suits, Appeals and Applications

sections.section_title: Exclusion of time in legal proceedings
sections.text: In computing the period of limitation for any suit, appeal or application, the day from which such period is to be reckoned shall be excluded. In computing the period of limitation for an appeal or application for leave to appeal or for revision, the time requisite for obtaining a copy of the judgment, decree, order or sentence appealed from or sought to be revised shall also be excluded.
sections.chapter: III — Computation of Period of Limitation

sections.section_title: Exclusion of time in cases where leave to sue or appeal as a pauper is applied for
sections.text: In computing the period of limitation for any suit or appeal in which leave to sue or appeal as a pauper is applied for, the time taken from the date of the application to the date of the order rejecting it shall be excluded, and the time taken for any proceedings in court for the grant of such leave shall also be excluded.
sections.chapter: III — Computation of Period of Limitation

sections.section_title: Exclusion of time of proceeding bona fide in court without jurisdiction
sections.text: In computing the period of limitation for any suit or application, the time during which the plaintiff or applicant has been prosecuting with due diligence another civil proceeding, whether in a court of first instance or of appeal or revision, against the defendant or respondent, shall be excluded, where the proceeding relates to the same matter and is prosecuted in good faith in a court which, from defect of jurisdiction or other cause of a like nature, is unable to entertain it.
sections.chapter: III — Computation of Period of Limitation

sections.section_title: Exclusion of time when proceedings are stayed by injunction or order
sections.text: In computing the period of limitation for any suit or application for the execution of a decree, the time during which any proceeding for the execution of the decree has been stayed by injunction or order of a court shall be excluded. In computing the period of limitation for any suit, the time during which the defendant has been absent from India and from the territories outside India under the administration of the Central Government shall be excluded.
sections.chapter: III — Computation of Period of Limitation

sections.section_title: Effect of death on period of limitation
sections.text: Where a person who would, if he were living, have a right to institute a suit or make an application dies before the expiration of the period prescribed, the period of limitation shall be reckoned from the time when there is a legal representative capable of instituting the suit or making the application.
sections.chapter: III — Computation of Period of Limitation

sections.section_title: Effect of fraud or mistake
sections.text: Where any person having a right to institute a suit or make an application has, by means of fraud, been kept from the knowledge of such right or of the title on which it is founded, or where any document necessary to establish such right has been fraudulently concealed, the time limited for instituting the suit or making the application shall be computed from the time when the fraud or concealment became known to the plaintiff or applicant, or could with reasonable diligence have been known.
sections.chapter: III — Computation of Period of Limitation

sections.section_title: Effect of acknowledgement in writing
sections.text: Where, before the expiration of the prescribed period for a suit or application in respect of any debt or other right, an acknowledgement of liability in writing signed by the party against whom such right is claimed, or by his authorised agent, is made, a fresh period of limitation shall be computed from the time when the acknowledgement was made.
sections.chapter: III — Computation of Period of Limitation

sections.section_title: Effect of payment on account of debt or of interest on legacy
sections.text: Where payment on account of a debt or of interest on a legacy is made before the expiration of the prescribed period by the person liable to pay or by his authorised agent, a fresh period of limitation shall be computed from the time when the payment was made.
sections.chapter: III — Computation of Period of Limitation

sections.section_title: Effect of acknowledgement or payment by another person
sections.text: The acknowledgement or payment referred to in sections 18 and 19 may be made by the person liable or by his authorised agent, and shall bind the principal and other persons interested in the estate, but not a person who has already parted with his interest without notice.
sections.chapter: III — Computation of Period of Limitation

sections.section_title: Effect of substituting or adding new plaintiff or defendant
sections.text: Where, after the period of limitation for a suit has expired, a new plaintiff or defendant is substituted or added, the suit shall, as regards him, be deemed to have been instituted on the date when he was so made a party.
sections.chapter: III — Computation of Period of Limitation

sections.section_title: Continuing breaches and torts
sections.text: In the case of a continuing breach of contract or a continuing tort, a fresh period of limitation begins to run at every moment of the time during which the breach or tort, as the case may be, continues.
sections.chapter: III — Computation of Period of Limitation

sections.section_title: Suits for compensation for acts not actionable without special damage
sections.text: In the case of a suit for compensation for an act which is not actionable without special damage, the period of limitation shall be computed from the time when the act results in actual damage.
sections.chapter: III — Computation of Period of Limitation

sections.section_title: Computation of time mentioned in instruments
sections.text: All instruments shall, for the purposes of this Act, be deemed to be made with reference to the Gregorian calendar.
sections.chapter: III — Computation of Period of Limitation

sections.section_title: Acquisition of easement by prescription
sections.text: Where the access and use of light or air to and for any building have been peaceably enjoyed without interruption for twenty years, and where any way or watercourse or the use of any water or any other easement has been peaceably and openly enjoyed without interruption for twenty years, the right to such access or use shall be absolute and indefeasible.
sections.chapter: IV — Miscellaneous

sections.section_title: Exclusion in favour of reversioner of servient tenement
sections.text: Where any land or water upon, over or from which any easement has been enjoyed or derived is subject to a tenancy, the time during which the tenant was in possession shall, for the purposes of section 25, be excluded in computing the twenty-year period if the claim is made against the reversioner.
sections.chapter: IV — Miscellaneous

sections.section_title: Extinguishment of right to property
sections.text: At the determination of the period hereby limited to any person for instituting a suit for possession of any property, his right to such property shall be extinguished.
sections.chapter: IV — Miscellaneous

sections.section_title: Amendment of First Schedule
sections.text: The First Schedule to the Indian Limitation Act, 1908, is hereby amended in the manner specified in the Schedule to this Act. [Note: Section 28 has since been repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1969 (Act 10 of 1969).]
sections.chapter: IV — Miscellaneous

sections.section_title: Savings
sections.text: Nothing in this Act shall affect any suit, appeal or application instituted, preferred or made before the commencement of this Act. Nothing in this Act shall apply to suits, appeals or applications relating to any matter for which limitation is expressly provided by any special or local law.
sections.chapter: IV — Miscellaneous

sections.section_title: Provision for suits, etc., for which the prescribed period is shorter than the period prescribed by the Indian Limitation Act, 1908
sections.text: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, where the period of limitation prescribed by this Act for any suit, appeal or application is shorter than the period prescribed by the Indian Limitation Act, 1908, the shorter period shall not apply to any suit, appeal or application if the period prescribed by the earlier Act had already expired before the commencement of this Act.
sections.chapter: IV — Miscellaneous

sections.section_title: Provisions as to certain cases under the Bombay, Madras and Bengal Acts
sections.text: [Section 31 provided transitional savings in respect of limitation periods under the repealed Bombay Limitation Act, 1869, the Madras Limitation Act, 1876 and the Bengal Limitation Act, 1864. This section has been omitted by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1974 (Act 56 of 1974).]
sections.chapter: IV — Miscellaneous

sections.section_title: Repeal
sections.text: The Indian Limitation Act, 1908, is hereby repealed.
sections.chapter: IV — Miscellaneous
